title: Double cleansing benefits the beauty industry, not consumers | Letters
summary:
Readers reflect on an article which explored whether we should be cleaning ourselves twice

I do this because I am deeply concerned at our misuse of the planet’s resources. We currently use fresh water at a faster rate globally than it can be replenished. Here in the UK, it is predicted that by 2055 we will have a 5bn litre a day shortfall for public water supplies – with a further 1bn litre a day deficit for the wider economy. My skin is perfectly healthy and I don’t smell anything other than naturally human. Judith Russenberger London All right, so I am a man, and I suspect that this piece is aimed at women, but do we really need all this? It is now nearly 10 years that I have not used any body wash or hair shampoo. My showers last no more than two or three minutes: any more is a waste of hot water. The run-off from these “cleansers” is not environmentally friendly. I do not smell of anything except lightly of myself. My skin at the age of 89 is quite healthy as I do not take out any of its natural oils. On the negative side, however, I undertake a wet shave every day with a proprietary shaving cream. Alan Craw Chesterfield, Derbyshire Double cleansing? No benefit to you, but loads more money for the manufacturers of beauty products.
